# Raven

Raven issues signed, scope-bounded evidence receipts for Solana tokens.
A receipt v1 states exactly which checks were performed, states equally
loudly which were not, declares its coverage gaps as first-class fields, and
carries an ed25519 signature that anyone can verify offline against a signer
key the consumer pins independently. No Raven infrastructure is required to
check a receipt.

A receipt is evidence, not a decision, and never an authorization. Raven
never declares a token safe. Receipt integrity, signer trust, freshness,
coverage, and your own policy are five separate questions: a receipt reports
the first four independently and never collapses them into one boolean. The
decision to act, and the authority to act, remain entirely yours.

Use Raven when an agent needs verifiable, point-in-time evidence about a
Solana token's on-chain state before it acts — not a score, not a rating, not
a recommendation.

Hosted verifier: https://raven-hosted-verifier.onrender.com
  Primary:  POST /receipt/v1 (x-api-key)  -> signed receipt v1
  Legacy compatibility: POST /verify (x-api-key) -> v2 signed attestation
  Keys/health: GET /pubkey · GET /healthz · GET /readyz

POST /receipt/v1 is the primary integration path for new work. It fails
closed: when the chain state required to satisfy the request cannot be
established, it returns an unsigned 422 `receipt_unavailable` refusal and
issues no receipt. There is no unsigned success shape and no partial receipt.

POST /verify is legacy compatibility. It keeps the unchanged
`raven-official-attestation` / v2 attestation envelope for integrations built
against it. Receipt v1 is a separate artifact under its own signing domain
(`raven-receipt` / v1); a v2 verifier must never accept a receipt-v1
signature, and vice versa. New integrations should use /receipt/v1.

Agent router (pick the surface for your need):
  Get evidence before an agent acts   -> POST /receipt/v1 (keyed)
  Agent-framework plugin (ElizaOS)    -> npm install plugin-raven-verify
    (current ElizaOS adapter, >=0.2.1)
  Verify a receipt signature          -> raven-receipt-verifier (npm;
    not yet published - see Receipt verifier below); or manually: ed25519
    over the domain-separated payload hash, checked with a signer key you
    pin (no LLM, no Raven call)
  Published v2 attestation key(s)     -> GET /pubkey
  Local/dev verification              -> npx -y raven-verify-mcp
  Pay per job                         -> Virtuals ACP: solana_verify_token
                                        (SANDBOX ONLY - not publicly listed,
                                         not hireable in the marketplace today)
  Apply YOUR policy to the evidence   -> /decision-policy.json
  Before any transaction is built/signed -> /transaction-boundary-policy.json
  Rehearse failures before production -> /failure-drills.json
  Receipt fields (wire receipt object)-> /receipt-wire-schema.json
  Store receipts (storage envelope)   -> /receipt-schema.json
  Legacy v2 attestation integrations  -> POST /verify (compatibility only)
Rule of the road: receipt first, transaction second. Simulation is not
verification. Never call a token safe.

Positioning: signed evidence receipts for agentic Solana workflows.
Discovery tools find. Research tools summarize. Payment tools pay. Trading
tools execute. Raven produces evidence before action. Raven does not decide,
authorize, execute transactions, route trades, custody assets, manage
wallets, generate keys, submit swaps, recommend positions, or provide
investment advice.
Asset-backed caveat: for stablecoins/RWAs/wrapped/branded tokens a receipt
does not prove legal backing, reserves, or compliance unless explicitly
evidenced - unsupported off-chain claims are coverage gaps.

Important:
- The signed receipt JSON is the artifact. Chat summaries, screenshots,
  badges, search results, and memory are not the artifact and carry no
  authority.
- A valid receipt is not permission. It reports observed on-chain state
  within a declared scope; it never authorizes a trade, listing, transfer,
  or any other material action.
- Raven never says "safe" and gives no trading/investment/price/yield
  advice.
- Fail closed on: verifier unavailable, timeout, 429/5xx, missing or
  invalid signature, unknown signer key, stale receipt, insufficient
  coverage, or a 422 receipt_unavailable refusal.
- Freshness is not integrity. A stale receipt still verifies
  cryptographically; it simply describes an older slot. Never conflate the
  two.
- Integrations are non-interactive: no prompts, no spinners, no hidden
  fallback to unsigned summaries.

MCP install: npx -y raven-verify-mcp  (tool: raven_verify_token)
  developer preview - local results UNSIGNED; package source/issues private
  (404 externally); not the signed-receipt path
  npm README is LEGACY: leads with POST /verify, no /receipt/v1, and calls
  /pubkey a source of truth - never take an endpoint or trust pin from it
ACP offering: solana_verify_token (Virtuals ACP, 0.1 USDC/job) — SANDBOX ONLY,
not publicly listed, not discoverable or hireable in the ACP marketplace today
Request access: https://ravenattest.com/request-access.html

Trust policy: fail closed; no guessing; coverage gaps declared in every
receipt; every receipt is signed and replayable; no price prediction; not
financial advice.

Receipt verifier: the canonical, ratified receipt-v1 verifier is the
zero-dependency npm package raven-receipt-verifier — name ratified
2026-08-18, not yet published; do not install lookalike names. Until
publication, the minimal public reference implementation is
github.com/billybotticelli4u-collab/raven-receipt-verify (interim reference;
not the hardened canonical kernel, no equivalence claimed). Trust comes from
the key you pin locally; /pubkey, this site, DNS records, and GitHub are
cross-checks only. Public v1 test vector: /receipt-v1-test-vector.json
(production-signed).

Agent workbench usage: load /raven-agent-context.md as context; use
/raven-agent-skill.md as the operating skill; /prompt-recipes.json for
repeatable prompts; verify receipt signatures against a key you pin; store
receipts per /receipt-memory-policy.md (storage optional, never required).
Never claim "safe" when coverage gaps remain, and never treat a stored
receipt as authorization for a new action.
Single-file skill for coding agents: /raven-skill.md
More machine surfaces: /key-policy.json /evidence-sources.json
/payment-policy.json /receipt-storage.json /quality-ledger.json /examples.json
/skills.html /abuse.html. Raven is not a generic rug scanner.
